topics.title: Mass — scaled instruments: Measure and compare masses using scales; read graduated scales to measure kg and g

questions.stem: If the nine sports items are numbered from smallest mass (1) to largest mass (9), which list correctly orders the four lightest items from smallest to largest?
options: Tennis ball (58 g), table tennis bat (85 g), badminton racquet (90 g), softball bat (94 g)
Tennis ball (58 g), badminton racquet (90 g), table tennis bat (85 g), softball bat (94 g)
Table tennis bat (85 g), tennis ball (58 g), badminton racquet (90 g), softball bat (94 g)
Tennis ball (58 g), table tennis bat (85 g), softball bat (94 g), badminton racquet (90 g)
questions.hint: Find all items under 100 g (58 g, 85 g, 90 g, 94 g) and order them from smallest to largest.

keyPoints.note: Convert kg to g (1 kg = 1000 g) so every item can be compared in grams.
Compare the four items under 100 g: 58 g, 85 g, 90 g, 94 g.

steps.explain: Convert the kilogram masses to grams so all 9 items are in the same unit: \(1\text{ kg} = 1000\text{ g}\) and \(5\text{ kg} = 5000\text{ g}\).

questions.stem: When all nine sports items are numbered from smallest mass (1) to largest mass (9), which item is number 5 (the middle mass)?
questions.hint: Convert 1 kg = 1000 g and 5 kg = 5000 g, list all 9 masses from smallest to largest, and pick the 5th one.

keyPoints.note: Rank all 9 items in grams from 1 to 9.
There are 4 lighter items and 4 heavier items than the 5th item.

questions.stem: Use the sports equipment masses to answer: Which item weighs more than \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) kg but less than \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) kg?
questions.hint: Convert both fractions of a kilogram to grams: 1/4 kg = 250 g and 1/2 kg = 500 g. Then find the item between 250 g and 500 g.

keyPoints.note: Remember 1 kg = 1000 g, 1/2 kg = 500 g, and 1/4 kg = 250 g.

questions.stem: A temperature starts at \(35^\circ\text{C}\) and changes by \(-8^\circ\text{C}\). What is the end temperature?
questions.hint: A negative change (-8 °C) means the temperature goes DOWN — subtract 8 from 35.

keyPoints.note: Up (+) means add; Down (−) means subtract.

steps.explain: Start at \(35^\circ\text{C}\). A change of \(-8^\circ\text{C}\) means subtracting \(8^\circ\text{C}\).
Calculate \(35 - 8 = 27\).
Check with the inverse operation: \(27 + 8 = 35\).
Therefore, the end temperature is \(27^\circ\text{C}\).

questions.stem: A temperature starts at \(5^\circ\text{C}\) and changes by \(+16^\circ\text{C}\). What is the end temperature?
questions.hint: A positive change (+16 °C) means the temperature goes UP — add 16 to 5.

keyPoints.note: Up (+) means add; Down (−) means subtract.

steps.explain: Start at \(5^\circ\text{C}\). A change of \(+16^\circ\text{C}\) means adding \(16^\circ\text{C}\).
Calculate \(5 + 16 = 21\).
Check with the inverse operation: \(21 - 16 = 5\).
Therefore, the end temperature is \(21^\circ\text{C}\).

questions.stem: A temperature starts at \(40^\circ\text{C}\) and changes by \(+21^\circ\text{C}\). What is the end temperature?
questions.hint: A positive change (+21 °C) means the temperature goes UP — add 21 to 40.

keyPoints.note: Up (+) means add; Down (−) means subtract.

steps.explain: Start at \(40^\circ\text{C}\). A change of \(+21^\circ\text{C}\) means adding \(21^\circ\text{C}\).
Calculate \(40 + 21 = 61\).
Check with the inverse operation: \(61 - 21 = 40\).
Therefore, the end temperature is \(61^\circ\text{C}\).

questions.stem: A temperature starts at \(100^\circ\text{C}\) and changes by \(-56^\circ\text{C}\). What is the end temperature?
questions.hint: A negative change (-56 °C) means the temperature goes DOWN — subtract 56 from 100.

keyPoints.note: Up (+) means add; Down (−) means subtract.

steps.explain: Start at \(100^\circ\text{C}\). A change of \(-56^\circ\text{C}\) means subtracting \(56^\circ\text{C}\).
Check with the inverse operation: \(44 + 56 = 100\).
Therefore, the end temperature is \(44^\circ\text{C}\).

questions.stem: A temperature starts at \(32^\circ\text{C}\) and changes by \(-12^\circ\text{C}\). What is the end temperature?
questions.hint: A negative change (-12 °C) means the temperature goes DOWN — subtract 12 from 32.

keyPoints.note: Up (+) means add; Down (−) means subtract.

steps.explain: Start at \(32^\circ\text{C}\). A change of \(-12^\circ\text{C}\) means subtracting \(12^\circ\text{C}\).
Calculate \(32 - 12 = 20\).
Check with the inverse operation: \(20 + 12 = 32\).
Therefore, the end temperature is \(20^\circ\text{C}\).

questions.stem: An elephant, a giraffe, and a hippo have a total mass of \(7700\text{ kg}\). The hippo has a mass of \(2000\text{ kg}\), and the elephant has a mass \(2.5\) times the mass of the hippo. What is the mass of the giraffe?
questions.hint: First find the elephant’s mass (2.5 × 2000 = 5000 kg), add the hippo (5000 + 2000 = 7000 kg), then subtract from 7700 kg.

keyPoints.note: Giraffe = 7700 - (hippo + elephant).

steps.explain: Find the elephant’s mass: \(2.5 \times 2000\text{ kg} = (2 \times 2000) + (0.5 \times 2000) = 4000 + 1000 = 5000\text{ kg}\).
Add the hippo’s mass and the elephant’s mass together.
Subtract \(7000\text{ kg}\) from the total mass (\(7700\text{ kg}\)) to find the giraffe.
Check: \(5000 + 2000 + 700 = 7700\text{ kg}\). The giraffe’s mass is 700 kg.

questions.stem: The \(2000\text{ kg}\) hippo is moved to a new zoo and loses \(45\text{ kg}\). What is the mass of the hippo in the new zoo?

keyPoints.note: Subtract 45 kg from 2000 kg.

steps.explain: Write the subtraction number sentence: \(2000 - 45\).

Check: \(1955 + 45 = 2000\text{ kg}\). The hippo’s new mass is 1955 kg.

questions.stem: How do you write "quarter past 7" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "o'clock" or "past" times, write the hour first, then a colon, then the two-digit minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: One quarter of 60 minutes is 15 minutes past 7.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write "25 past 8" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "o'clock" or "past" times, write the hour first, then a colon, then the two-digit minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: 25 past 8 means the hour is 8 and 25 minutes have passed.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write "quarter to 10" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "to" times, the digital hour is 1 less than the stated hour, and the minutes equal 60 minus the minutes to the hour.

keyPoints.note: Quarter to 10 is 15 minutes before 10:00, so the hour is still 9 and minutes = 60 - 15 = 45.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write "10 to 5" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "to" times, the digital hour is 1 less than the stated hour, and the minutes equal 60 minus the minutes to the hour.

keyPoints.note: 10 to 5 is 10 minutes before 5:00, so the hour is still 4 and minutes = 60 - 10 = 50.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

steps.explain: Visualise "10 to 5" on an analogue clock face to see where the hour hand and minute hand point.

questions.stem: How do you write "5 past 3" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "o'clock" or "past" times, write the hour first, then a colon, then the two-digit minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: 5 past 3 means hour 3 and 05 minutes (always write two digits for minutes!).
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

steps.explain: Visualise "5 past 3" on an analogue clock face to see where the hour hand and minute hand point.

questions.stem: How do you write "half past 1" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "o'clock" or "past" times, write the hour first, then a colon, then the two-digit minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes past 1.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write "20 to 8" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "to" times, the digital hour is 1 less than the stated hour, and the minutes equal 60 minus the minutes to the hour.

keyPoints.note: 20 to 8 is 20 minutes before 8:00, so the hour is still 7 and minutes = 60 - 20 = 40.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(9:00\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 0 minutes is 30 or less, read it as minutes PAST 9 (remember 15 = quarter past, 30 = half past, 00 = o'clock).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.
Use "past" up to 30 minutes and "to" the next hour after 30 minutes.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(9\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(00\)).

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(6:45\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 45 minutes is past half past (30), subtract 45 from 60 to find how many minutes TO the next hour (7).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.
Use "past" up to 30 minutes and "to" the next hour after 30 minutes.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(6\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(45\)).

questions.hint: Since 25 minutes is 30 or less, read it as minutes PAST 2 (remember 15 = quarter past, 30 = half past, 00 = o'clock).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(2\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(25\)).

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(8:50\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 50 minutes is past half past (30), subtract 50 from 60 to find how many minutes TO the next hour (9).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.
Use "past" up to 30 minutes and "to" the next hour after 30 minutes.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(8\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(50\)).

steps.explain: Because \(50 > 30\), we express the time as minutes TO the next hour (\(8 + 1 = 9\)).

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(2:20\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 20 minutes is 30 or less, read it as minutes PAST 2 (remember 15 = quarter past, 30 = half past, 00 = o'clock).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.
Use "past" up to 30 minutes and "to" the next hour after 30 minutes.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(2\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(20\)).

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(4:40\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 40 minutes is past half past (30), subtract 40 from 60 to find how many minutes TO the next hour (5).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(4\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(40\)).

questions.stem: What digital time is shown on this analogue clock?
questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(7\) and \(8\), which means the hour is still \(7\).

questions.stem: What digital time is shown on this analogue clock?
questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(4\) and \(5\), which means the hour is still \(4\).

steps.explain: Count \(2\) individual minute ticks past \(2\): \(10 + 2 = 12\) minutes.
Combine the hour (\(4\)) and minutes (\(12\)) to write the digital time \(4:12\).

questions.stem: What digital time is shown on this analogue clock?
questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(6\) and \(7\), which means the hour is still \(6\).

steps.explain: Count \(3\) individual minute ticks past \(8\): \(40 + 3 = 43\) minutes.
Combine the hour (\(6\)) and minutes (\(43\)) to write the digital time \(6:43\).

questions.stem: What digital time is shown on this analogue clock?
questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(1\) and \(2\), which means the hour is still \(1\).

steps.explain: Count \(1\) individual minute tick past \(5\): \(25 + 1 = 26\) minutes.
Combine the hour (\(1\)) and minutes (\(26\)) to write the digital time \(1:26\).

questions.stem: Convert 2 minutes into seconds.
questions.hint: Multiply by 60: multiply by 6 first, then place a 0 at the end.

keyPoints.note: Multiply by 60 (60 s = 1 min, 60 min = 1 hr).

steps.explain: Recall the time conversion rule: \(60\) seconds = \(1\) minute, and \(60\) minutes = \(1\) hour.
Multiply \(2\) by \(60\): first calculate \(2 \times 6 = 12\).
Attach the zero to get \(120\).
Therefore, 2 minutes equals 120 seconds.

questions.stem: The Maddock family went for a long walk last Saturday. They started out at \(8\) o'clock in the morning and finished at \(1\) o'clock in the afternoon. How many hours did the walk take?
questions.hint: Count forward from 8 o'clock to 12 o'clock (4 hours), then 1 more hour to 1 o'clock.

keyPoints.note: Count forward from 8 o'clock to 12 o'clock (4 hours), then 1 more hour to 1 o'clock.

steps.explain: Count forward from 8:00 am to 12:00 pm (noon): 12 - 8 = 4 hours.
Add 1 more hour from 12:00 pm to 1:00 pm.
Check by counting hour by hour: 9, 10, 11, 12, 1 (5 hours).
Therefore, the walk took 5 hours.

questions.stem: The Maddock family's walk lasted \(5\) hours (from \(8\) o'clock to \(1\) o'clock). How many minutes did the walk take?
questions.hint: Convert 5 hours into minutes by multiplying 5 × 60.

keyPoints.note: Convert 5 hours into minutes by multiplying 5 × 60.

steps.explain: Recall that 1 hour = 60 minutes.
Multiply 5 hours by 60 minutes: 5 × 6 = 30, then attach 0.
Check by repeated addition: 60 + 60 + 60 + 60 + 60 = 300.
Therefore, the walk took 300 minutes.

questions.stem: In 2016, Aleix Vendrell held the world record for holding his breath for \(24\) minutes! For how many seconds did Aleix hold his breath?
questions.hint: Multiply 24 minutes by 60 seconds: split 24 into 20 + 4, multiply each by 60, and add them.

keyPoints.note: Multiply 24 minutes by 60 seconds: split 24 into 20 + 4, multiply each by 60, and add them.

steps.explain: Convert 24 minutes into seconds by multiplying 24 × 60.
Split 24 into 20 + 4 and multiply each part by 60: 20 × 60 = 1200 and 4 × 60 = 240.
Add the two partial products: 1200 + 240 = 1440 seconds.
Therefore, Aleix held his breath for 1440 seconds.

questions.stem: Mandy's dental appointment was at \(5:00\text{ pm}\). She arrived at the dentist at \(4:40\text{ pm}\). Was she early or late, and by how many minutes?
questions.hint: Compare 4:40 pm with 5:00 pm: 4:40 pm comes BEFORE 5:00 pm (early), and 60 - 40 = 20 minutes remain until 5:00 pm.

keyPoints.note: Compare 4:40 pm with 5:00 pm: 4:40 pm comes BEFORE 5:00 pm (early), and 60 - 40 = 20 minutes remain until 5:00 pm.

steps.explain: Compare the arrival time (4:40 pm) with the appointment time (5:00 pm): 4:40 pm is earlier than 5:00 pm, so Mandy was early.
Find how many minutes from 4:40 pm to 5:00 pm using 1 hour = 60 minutes.
Check: 4:40 pm + 20 minutes = 5:00 pm.
Therefore, Mandy was early by 20 minutes.

questions.stem: Reece thought his dental appointment was \(25\) minutes later than the actual appointment, which was at \(12:30\text{ pm}\). What time did Reece think his appointment was?
questions.hint: Add 25 minutes to 12:30 pm: 30 + 25 = 55 minutes past 12.

keyPoints.note: Add 25 minutes to 12:30 pm: 30 + 25 = 55 minutes past 12.

steps.explain: Start from the actual appointment time: 12:30 pm.
Add 25 minutes to the minutes part (30 minutes).
Since 55 is less than 60, the hour stays 12 pm, giving 12:55 pm.
Therefore, Reece thought his appointment was at 12:55 pm.

keyPoints.note: Add 45 minutes to 11:15 am: 15 + 45 = 60 minutes = 1 full hour, taking 11:00 am to 12:00 pm (noon)!

steps.explain: Start from the appointment time: 11:15 am.
Add 45 minutes to the 15 minutes: 15 + 45 = 60 minutes.
Add that 1 full hour to 11:00 am: 11:00 am + 1 hour = 12:00 pm (noon).
Therefore, Ellissa arrived at 12:00 pm (noon).
